loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>

user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>

</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.\nDaisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"\nAssistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.\nDaisy: "Please review PR #1234"\nAssistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.\nDaisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"\nAssistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example> (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)
- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)
- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

**As a** Site Merchandiser, I want to manage SEO text content in Contentful per category, so that it can be updated per storefront without a code deployment.

=== README.md contentful (head 40) ===
# Contentful tooling

Zimmermann uses **two different Contentful surfaces**. Keep them straight — they live in different places and are managed by different tools.

## 1. Content types (editorial schemas)

**What:** Schemas for editorial entries authors fill in (e.g. `footerConfig`, `link`).
**Where:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` — plain JS, one file per content type. This is the **sole** source of truth for a content type's fields, including `required`/`localized`/`validations` — there is no separate migration file layered on top.
**How:** Pushed as one organization-scoped **Environment Template**, then installed into each environment. This is Contentful's current recommended mechanism — content models are authored once at the organization level, not created independently per space/environment (see the `contentful-management` SDK's `client.environmentTemplate.*` API).

```bash
npm run sync:contentful                                   # build/update the template from content-types/*.js
npm run install:contentful -- --target dev                # push it into one environment
npm run install:contentful -- --target dev --dry-run       # validate only, no changes
```

Driven by [buildTemplate.js](./buildTemplate.js) (assembles `content-types/*.js` into one
`EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`) and
[setup/installTemplate.mjs](./setup/installTemplate.mjs) (validates then installs the
template's current version into `--target <environmentId>`, polling until the install
reaches a terminal status). Reads `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`,
and `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` from `.env`.

Promotion order: `dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master` — run `install:contentful`
against each target in turn. Contentful tracks each environment's install status/version
natively (`environmentTemplateInstallation`) — there's no hand-rolled migration-history
content type and no separate drift-detection script, since every environment installs
from the same versioned template and can't drift from it the way independently-synced
environments used to.

**Entries are a separate concern from the template.** Environment Templates cover
content-*type* schema only — seed data (e.g. the canonical `region` entries) needs its
own per-environment script, run after that environment has the relevant content type
installed:

```bash
npm run seed:contentful-regions -- --target dev
```

See [setup/seedRegions.mjs](./setup/seedRegions.mjs).

SPACE=$(grep -h '^CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID=' .env | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"'"'"' ')
echo "space=$SPACE"
for TIER in dev test sit staging uat prod; do
  f=".env.$TIER"
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  ENVID=$(grep -h '^CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=' "$f" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"'"'"' ')
  TOK=$(grep -h '^CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN=' "$f" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '"'"'"' ')
  if [ -z "$ENVID" ] || [ -z "$TOK" ]; then echo "$TIER: (no env id or token in $f)"; continue; fi
  ENTRIES=$(curl -s --max-time 20 "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/$SPACE/environments/$ENVID/entries?limit=1&access_token=$TOK" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(d.get('total', d.get('message','ERR')))" 2>/dev/null)
  TYPES=$(curl -s --max-time 20 "https://cdn.contentful.com/spaces/$SPACE/environments/$ENVID/content_types?limit=100&access_token=$TOK" | python3 -c "import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);items=d.get('items');print(str(d.get('total'))+' :: '+','.join(sorted(i['sys']['id'] for i in items)) if items is not None else d.get('message','ERR'))" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "$TIER (env=$ENVID): entries=$ENTRIES"
  echo "     types=$TYPES"
done

content.text:
Both pages read in full (no truncation). Report below.

## 1. The content-model list — the "8" quote is real but **stale**

The quoted snippet is verbatim from the **decision log on 5.9 — Contentful Migration** (page 465076226, version 12), row dated `2026-09-02`:

> | 2026-09-02 | Content model set finalised at 8: Editorial Card, Simple Text, Rich Text, Accordion/FAQ Item, Boutique, Style Guide Item, Table, Pull Quote | Card merged into Editorial Card; Document Page-Image Set dropped (it's just a gallery) |

5.9's working-areas table repeats it:

> | [5.9.2 — Content Model Mapping](…/465240068) | The actual Contentful content models we need (no "Page" content type — pages are composed in Studio) | In progress — 8 models identified, refined against real Magento data |

**But 5.9.2 itself (version 41 — far more heavily revised than 5.9's version 12) now has a section literally headed "The 12 content models":**

> Hero · Editorial Card · Simple Text · Rich Text · Accordion · Boutique · Table · Pull Quote · Media Collection · Look · Video · ShoppableProduct

Deltas against the "8" list:
- **`Style Guide Item` is no longer a model.** Verbatim from 5.9.2: *"**Style Guide Item** is not its own model — it's Editorial Card with the image aligned left instead of on top (`imageAlignment`: Left). This hasn't yet been checked against a real style-guide Figma frame — see Open items below."*
- **Added since:** Hero, Media Collection, Look, Video, ShoppableProduct.
- **Plus 4 more** under *"Global shell & configuration models (already shipped)"*: Footer Config, Header Navigation, Header Nav Item, UI Copy — explicitly *"a different category from the 12 above — they're not part of the 300-page Magento migration inventory."*

So the current agreed set is **12 migration models + 4 already-shipped global/config models**, not 8. The two pages contradict each other; 5.9's decision-log row and status column are an un-updated 2026-09-02 snapshot.

## 2. Breadcrumb — **no** breadcrumb content type exists

Breadcrumb appears **only as a component with no backing model**, and only on 5.9.2. Verbatim, from the "Every component maps to a model" table:

> | Breadcrumb | Likely derived from the page's own position/hierarchy rather than authored content — to confirm. Supports 3+ hierarchy levels (e.g. Home / About / Acknowledgement of Country) |

5.9.2 Open items:

> * Whether Breadcrumb is genuinely the one component with no backing content model, or should also map to something authored

5.9 Open items:

> * Whether Breadcrumb is genuinely derived-not-authored, the way Back/Next Nav turned out not to be

Only other mention, in "How pages are typically composed" (5.9.2):

> * **Article/editorial pages** (most of Z.Immerse) are a hero, breadcrumb, rich text, image galleries, and occasionally a pull quote or a shoppable product carousel.

Note the phrase *"the one component with no backing content model"* — Breadcrumb is singled out as the sole unmapped component on the entire page.

## 3. SEO — **nothing**. No SEO content type, no SEO section

There is **no occurrence of "SEO", "SEO copy", "SEO text", or "category SEO"** anywhere in 5.9.2's body — not in the 12-model list, not in the 4 global/config models, not in the component-mapping table, not in Open items.

On 5.9, "SEO" appears **only as part of a PRD filename**, twice, and both times about redirects, not content modelling:

> * Redirect mapping ownership (PRD `dataMigrationSeo.md` DMU-018) — still Open

> * `.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md` doesn't currently reflect this CMS content-page migration scope at all

(Caveat on method: CQL `text ~ "SEO"` scoped to both page IDs returned empty, but so did `text ~ "dataMigrationSeo"` on a page that demonstrably contains that string — so CQL tokenisation is unreliable here. The negative above rests on my full read of both page bodies, which is the authoritative check.)

## 4. SFCC-748 / SFCC-749 / "Breadcrumb and SEO" — **not mentioned on either page**

Neither page references either key or that phrase. Jira keys that *are* cited: SFCC-10 (epic), SFCC-873 (migration script), SFCC-531, SFCC-532, SFCC-547, SFCC-538, SFCC-542, SFCC-549, SFCC-536, SFCC-52, SFCC-55.

A space-wide CQL search for `text ~ "Breadcrumb and SEO"` returned **zero results** — the phrase does not appear anywhere in Confluence. Searches for the two keys were inconclusive at space scope (CQL splits `SFCC-748` on the hyphen and matches every page containing "SFCC"), but the page-scoped searches were clean and my direct read confirms absence on both.

The closest 5.9.2 gets to a "revisit the stories" statement is about two *different* tickets:

> SFCC-531 and SFCC-532 were scoped before this content-model review and lean toward one content type per page. Both should be updated to reflect the composable-component approach in this document — see 5.9.3's gap analysis for the detail.

## 5. Contentful vs SFCC Business Manager for category/PLP SEO copy — **not addressed at all**

Neither page contains the phrase "Business Manager", and neither discusses where category or PLP SEO copy should live. There is no verbatim quote to give because the question is simply never raised on either page.

The only PLP mention on either page is incidental, in 5.9's Open items:

> * `spring-26-cloud91-line` — real content, but the live URL redirects to a PLP — client to decide: preserve as archived content, or drop?

Both pages are scoped explicitly to **Magento CMS page migration** — *"roughly 300 Magento CMS pages into Contentful"* — which is a different surface from category/PLP merchandising copy. The one related boundary decision 5.9.2 does record is about a banner, not SEO:

> * Two items decided **not** to model as Contentful content: a sitewide announcement/promo banner (already covered by the SFCC platform team), and the Brand Protection "Report a Counterfeit" form (a one-off custom component, not authorable content) — see 5.9.3 for detail

---

### Bottom line for whoever is scoping SFCC-748/749

- Quoting "8 models" as the current agreed set would be wrong — 5.9.2 supersedes it with 12 (+4 shipped global/config). 5.9's decision log and status column need correcting.
- There is **no breadcrumb content type and no SEO content type** in the agreed model set, on either page.
- Breadcrumb is explicitly flagged as *probably derived, not authored* — but it's an **open question on both pages**, not a settled decision.
- The Contentful-vs-Business-Manager question for category/PLP SEO copy is **unanswered in this page tree**. If SFCC-748/749 depend on it, that's a genuine documentation gap, not something to infer from these two pages. Worth checking `.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md` (which 5.9 itself flags as out of date) and 5.9.3 / 5.9.3a before concluding.

No files written; no Confluence or Jira writes performed.

# SFCC-748 Backlog Refinement — Analysis

## Headline

**SFCC-748 is not ready, has never been pointed, and its core premise is contradicted by three confirmed sources. It should not be built as written.** The work it describes is also already specced twice elsewhere, by a different squad, in a different epic, with the opposite storage decision.

---

## Ticket state (verbatim)

**SFCC-748** — "Breadcrumb and SEO – Contentful Component" · epic SFCC-3 (Navigation) · status **Tech design** · Sprint 6 · reporter **Isabel Chaloner** · created 2026-08-17 · **labels `["Config", "Squad-A"]`** (note: `Config`, not `Custom` — and **no DMU requirement label**, unlike every Squad-B SEO sibling).

**Story points: never set.** Across all **53 changelog entries** there is not one story-point field change. This isn't "points were removed" — they were never entered.

**Acceptance criteria** (`customfield_10231`, verbatim — 4 ACs):

> \# Given the Contentful content type is created, when a Site Merchandiser opens the content model, then it includes category ID (mandatory), title (optional), intro text (optional), expanded SEO body (optional), and locale support.
> \# Given a Site Merchandiser creates a new entry, when they complete only the category ID field, then the entry is valid and can be published — all other fields are optional.
> \# Given a Site Merchandiser creates or updates a Contentful entry, when they author content for a specific locale, then the content is independently managed per locale and changes to one locale do not affect another.
> \# Given a Site Merchandiser updates and publishes a Contentful entry for a category, when the page loads after publishing, then the updated content is reflected without a code deployment.

**Issue links:** one only — `relates to SFCC-749`. No link to any Squad-B SEO ticket.

**Attachments:** 2 Figma screenshots (`image-20260830-234504.png`, `image-20260830-234554.png`), both uploaded by Isabel Chaloner 2026-08-31.

**Design/Technical Notes:** set 2026-09-15 by Isabel — a Figma Design System 2026 link (`node-id=40007614-112495`).

**Changelog — the churn is the story.** Status went `To Do → In Refinement` (2026-08-17) `→ Ready For Review` (08-31) `→ Tech design` (09-03) `→ Blocked` (09-07) `→ Tech design` (2026-09-22 01:18). Assignee went Marcel → Kiera Rikard-Bell → Hazel Cacalda → **back to Marcel**. Sprint went `None → 6 → 7 → 6`.

**The last four changes all happened within 17 seconds on 2026-09-22 01:18** — assignee to Marcel, sprint back to 6, DoR checklist expanded from 3 items to 7, status unblocked from `Blocked` to `Tech design`. Nothing in the ticket changed substantively; it was administratively unblocked and handed to you.

**Comments — the open question was never answered:**
> Hazel Marie Cacalda (2026-09-07): "can you confirm that the link in the Design field is the final approved version?"
> Isabel Chaloner (2026-09-15): "added"

"Added" answers a different question than "is it approved."

---

## C. THE CENTRAL VERDICT

**Yes — clearly. SFCC-748 builds a Contentful content type that the confirmed PRD says should live in SFCC/Business Manager.** Three independent confirmed sources say BM/SFCC; one unconfirmed Jira story says Contentful.

**Evidence 1** — `.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md` line 57, verbatim (confirmed):
> - CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level (DMU-035, partial resolution 2026-05-15): **SEO rules and attributes will live in SFCC per storefront** (not Contentful). Still Open: Sparro to define field schema before custom build.

**Evidence 2** — same file, line 81 (Open Items), which I found and you didn't cite:
> - CMS-editable on-page SEO field — field schema to be defined by Sparro (DMU-035, **location resolved as SFCC**)

This is the stronger quote. Line 57 says "partial resolution"; line 81 says the *location* specifically is **resolved**. What remains open is only the field schema, owed by Sparro.

**Evidence 3** — `.docs/prd/plp.md`, under `### 1.2 Editorial / SEO Content (SPR-03, SPR-04 — Confirmed 2026-05-08)`:
> - Configurable title, description, and hero image per category page **via Business Manager.**

⚠️ **Correction to your brief:** that's **line 19**, not line 18. Line 18 is the "read more" line. Substance holds, cite is off by one.

**Evidence 4** — Confluence 478248974 ("04.1.19 Data Migration / SEO / Analytics Requirements - Mapping"), the authoritative requirement→story map, verbatim:
> | DMU-036 | SEO | The system will provide a CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on all category and PLP pages, configurable at individual storefront level. | SFCC-22 (SEO & Analytics & A/B Testing) | **SFCC-577 — PLP SEO Copy Content Field (CMS-Editable, BM-Configurable)** | No PLP override or Contentful wiring exists yet — net-new build. See comment on SFCC-577. |

**SFCC-748 does not appear anywhere in that mapping table.** The requirement is mapped to SFCC-577 alone.

⚠️ **New finding — DMU numbering has drifted between sources.** This requirement is **DMU-035** in the local PRD but **DMU-036** in Confluence (where DMU-036 locally is `robots.txt`). Identical requirement text, different IDs. Worse: **the Confluence version omits the "(not Contentful)" resolution entirely.** So whichever source someone reads determines whether they think this decision exists. That alone explains how 748 got written.

**Evidence 5** — Confluence 5.9.2 / 5.9 (Contentful content-model pages). The agreed model set is *"The 12 content models"* — Hero, Editorial Card, Simple Text, Rich Text, Accordion, Boutique, Table, Pull Quote, Media Collection, Look, Video, ShoppableProduct — plus 4 shipped global models (Footer Config, Header Navigation, Header Nav Item, UI Copy). **There is no SEO content type and no breadcrumb content type on that list.** Breadcrumb appears only as a component with no backing model:
> | Breadcrumb | Likely derived from the page's own position/hierarchy rather than authored content — to confirm. |

**The honest counterweight, which matters:** the team is already drifting toward Contentful *regardless of the PRD*, and nobody has recorded the change.
- **SFCC-749 is 5 points and already "Ready for Development"** with 13 ACs that assume Contentful throughout. Someone signed that off.
- **SFCC-95** (Squad-B, epic SFCC-22 — the *same* epic as the BM-titled SFCC-577) says verbatim: *"The section headings and body copy are **CMS-managed in Contentful** and are page-contextual."*
- Tim Lavelle's comment on SFCC-577 itself (2026-09-11) discusses **Contentful** modelling, not BM: *"The Rich Text/Simple Text Contentful primitives from the CMS migration work already exist though, which cuts down the content-modelling side of this."*

So Squad-B's own two tickets **contradict each other** — SFCC-577's title says BM-Configurable, SFCC-95's body says Contentful. This is not "748 is wrong and everyone else is right." It's **an unrecorded decision reversal that nobody has written down anywhere**, and the PRD is the only artefact still holding the original line. Per AGENTS.md's Doc-integrity rule this is a hard stop: cite the doc, ask whether the doc is stale or the ticket is wrong, don't proceed either way.

---

## A. Seven-point sizing lens

1. **Front-end impact — effectively none.** The deliverable is `scripts/contentful/content-types/<name>.js`, which is outside `overrides/` and renders nothing. No component, no route, no bundle change. All visible behaviour lives in SFCC-749.
2. **Requirement clear enough to size? The ACs, yes. The premise, no.** The 4 ACs are unambiguous and directly implementable. But one of them is already wrong (see the storefront-scoping gap in section B), and the whole story may be building the wrong storage layer.
3. **Which surfaces —** none directly. Indirectly: category/PLP pages. The breadcrumb half of the title touches every page but explicitly needs **no** Contentful (*"The breadcrumb is programmatically generated by the PWA Kit and does not require Contentful authoring"*), so the title oversells the scope.
4. **Design/Figma dependencies — present but irrelevant, and unconfirmed.** A schema story consumes no Figma. The design link's approval status was asked on 09-07 and never actually answered.
5. **API/backend dependencies — real.** Needs `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` + `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` (tier-1-approver held), then `install:contentful` across **6 environments** (dev→test→sit→staging→uat→master). Plus Sparro still owes the field schema per the PRD's own Open Items.
6. **Pure FE / shared / needs architecture input → needs architecture input.** Two decisions above a FED's authority: Contentful-vs-BM, and how storefront scoping works.
7. **Sizeable now or blocked → BLOCKED.** Not on effort — on a product decision.

---

## B. Four axes

- **Behaviour — ambiguous, and two ACs collide across the pair.** 748 AC2 makes an entry with *only* a category ID valid and publishable. 749 AC3 only handles *"no published Contentful entry"* → render nothing. **Neither story covers "published but empty entry"** — which 748 explicitly permits. That renders an empty container, exactly what 749 AC3 was written to prevent.
- **Desktop/mobile — genuinely N/A.** A Contentful schema has no viewport. Correctly absent from the ACs; don't ask for it in refinement.
- **A11y — genuinely N/A for 748.** All 5 a11y ACs (nav/aria-label, keyboard, screen reader, reduced motion) correctly sit on SFCC-749. Nothing missing here.
- **Data — this is the whole story, and there's a concrete schema bug.** Beyond Contentful-vs-BM: the requirement demands *"configurable at individual storefront level"* and 748's own description says *"per storefront"* — **but AC1 lists no storefront/region field. Only locale.** Locale is not storefront: Zimmermann runs 8 storefronts across 11 locales, and AU/US-domestic/US-international can collide on a shared locale. This repo **already solved this and 748 re-opens it** — `footerConfig.js` carries a `regions` array precisely because locale alone was insufficient:
  > `// Omitted/empty = the default/global footer for its locale. A narrower-scoped entry (e.g. regions: [ZimmermannUS]) takes precedence over this one when resolving which footerConfig to render for a given site.`

  As written, 748 cannot satisfy the requirement it cites.

**Bonus contradiction, Confirmed PRD vs SFCC-749.** `plp.md` line 18 (SPR-03/04, Confirmed):
> Editorial/SEO paragraph with a "read more" expand action (**not collapsible** — confirmed per 24.06 design review)

SFCC-749 AC6, verbatim:
> Given the SEO text component is in its expanded state, when a shopper clicks READ LESS, then the component collapses back to the default state…

A confirmed design review says one-way expand; the 5-point story that's already Ready for Development specs a collapse. That's on 749, not 748, but it's the same pair and the same root cause.

---

## D. Codebase reality

**(i) Exists and reusable — more than expected:**

| Asset | Path | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| `useContentfulEntries<T>(contentType, preview, locale, filter)` | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentful.ts:185` | **Already exactly the right shape.** `filter` takes raw Contentful search syntax (`fields.categoryId=<id>`) and `locale` is already wired. Zero hook work needed. |
| `useContentfulClient` | `overrides/app/hooks/useContentfulClient.ts:35` | SDK-client alternative; used by footer + `useHeaderNav` |
| Content-type pipeline | `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js`, `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` | Org-scoped Environment Template; `npm run sync:contentful` then `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` |
| Category-ID resolution | `overrides/app/pages/categoryPath/index.tsx` | Already derives category from path via `categoryIdFromPathSegments` + `useCategory` — **this is both 748's keying source and 749's breadcrumb hierarchy source, already built** |
| PLP override | `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (45 KB) | Exists |
| Base breadcrumb | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/breadcrumb/index.jsx` | Available to copy-first |
| Region-scoping precedent | `scripts/contentful/content-types/footerConfig.js` | The `regions` pattern 748 is missing |

⚠️ **Tim Lavelle's SFCC-577 comment is now stale.** He wrote (2026-09-11): *"there's no override for the PLP/category page at all yet (no product-list folder under our overrides)."* `overrides/app/pages/product-list/` **exists** — first commit `3a5f756d`, 2026-09-07, four days *before* his comment. His broader point survives though: **`grep` confirms zero Contentful usage and zero breadcrumb in the PLP override.**

**(ii) Must be built from scratch:**
- The content-type file — **the only real deliverable**
- No breadcrumb override, no `overrides/app/components/seo` override
- No breadcrumb or SEO content type in **any** Contentful environment (verified live, all 6)

**Two things you can strike off the plan:**
- **Studio Experiences registration is NOT needed.** `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` is `defineComponents([])` and this is an editorial content type, not a Studio component.
- **`overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` (Tier 1) does NOT need touching.** I read it: it holds space ID, tokens, environment, and host constants only — nothing per-content-type. **No Tier 1 file is involved in this story at all.**

**Governance gate:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/` is **Tier 2** — *"Contentful Schema Definitions (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)"*. Notify, don't freeze. Note the warning: *"a mistaken field definition pushed to the production Contentful environment is difficult to undo and may break running components."*

**Real-world cost signal (step 5) — this is where the ladder breaks:**

The most recent net-new content types were `iconAndText.js` (56 lines) + `iconAndTextItem.js` (~40 lines), added in commit `df77a709` (2026-09-17, Jhoan Dela Cruz). That commit touched 16 files / 745 insertions — **but only 67 of those lines were content-type definitions (~9%)**; the rest was the component, stories, tests, theme and types.

In 4 months, **only 16 commits have ever touched `content-types/`**, and every one added the type as a side-effect of a component commit. A content type has never been a standalone multi-day effort in this repo.

⚠️ **Contrary evidence to your stated ladder.** You gave SFCC-912 = 3 as the Contentful-content-type benchmark. It's real, but there are two *closer* comparables you didn't have:

| Ticket | Points | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-117 "Footer — Contentful Component"** | **1** | Ready for SIT |
| **SFCC-835 "Icon and Text - Contentful Component Model"** | **2** | Ready for SIT |
| SFCC-912 "Footer — Contentful Component: **Development & Testing**" | 3 | Done |
| SFCC-750 "Footer - PWA Kit Component" | 8 | Ready for SIT |

SFCC-117 is the exact same shape as 748 (footer content type, nothing else) and was **1 point**. SFCC-835 delivered **two** content types plus TS types and was **2**. SFCC-912's higher 3 buys the *"Development & Testing"* in its title — broader scope than schema-only. **So "3 = a Contentful content-type story" is not what the board actually paid.**

**Step 7 — Contentful environment state. Your note is stale; corrected live today:**

| Env | Entries | Types |
|---|---|---|
| dev | **148** | 14 |
| test | **100** | 10 |
| sit | **97** | 9 |
| uat | **38** | 6 |
| staging | **0** | 6 |
| prod | *uncheckable* | — |

So "~38 entries across test/sit/uat" is true of **uat only**; test and sit are 100 and 97. Staging is genuinely empty. Code defines **10** types; dev has **14** (extras not in code: `collectionPageExp`, `richtext`, `sizeGuide`, `sizeGuideTable`), sit has a stray `zimmermann`. **staging and uat still carry the pre-unification `footerNavGroup`** — they never received the `navGroup` unification (`d934ad96`, 2026-08-26) and are ~1 month behind the template. That's a real promotion-debt item independent of this story, and it means "install the new type everywhere" is not a clean run today.

---

## E. Duplication / overlap

**This work is specced three times across two squads and two epics.**

| Ticket | Epic | Squad | Status | Pts | Claims to own |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-748** | SFCC-3 Navigation | A | Tech design | **none** | Contentful content type for category SEO text |
| **SFCC-749** | SFCC-3 Navigation | A | Ready for Dev | 5 | Breadcrumb + SEO text PWA component |
| **SFCC-577** | SFCC-22 SEO | B | To Do | none | *"CMS-Editable, **BM-Configurable**"* SEO copy field (label `DMU-036`) |
| **SFCC-95** | SFCC-22 SEO | B | To Do | none | Read-more SEO block, *"CMS-managed in **Contentful**"* (Bianca Morley; `SPR-03`, `SPR-61`, `DesignDependent`) |
| **SFCC-578** | SFCC-22 SEO | B | To Do | none | Breadcrumb component (PLP & PDP) (`DMU-034`, `DMU-039`) |
| **SFCC-579** | SFCC-22 SEO | B | To Do | none | Keyword tag links in SEO accordion (`DMU-036`) |
| **SFCC-573** | SFCC-22 SEO | B | To Do | none | CollectionPage/BreadcrumbList/ItemList schema (`DMU-039`) |

**Are SFCC-577 and SFCC-748 the same story told two ways? Substantially yes — but 577 is the one with provenance.**
- Same requirement: CMS-editable on-page SEO content field on category/PLP pages, per storefront.
